what_it_is: Identity security platform for humans, NHIs and AI agents, with ITDR and an MCP Gateway.
identity_note: Unosecur (unosecur.com), Berlin-based, with the Unified Identity Fabric, MCP Gateway and Ark AI. The MCP Gateway page also calls the gateway Ark AI.

1.reason: Finds agents across AWS Bedrock, Vertex, Copilot Studio, endpoints and repos. AI misconfiguration checks are identity-centric.
1.evidence: AI apps and coding agents on managed devices, found through device management and EDR.
1.has: AI Agent Security inventories agents on Bedrock, Vertex, Copilot Studio, endpoints, repos.
1.lacks: No model or notebook posture checks. No CI/CD or supply-chain scanning.

2.reason: MCP Gateway inventories servers and enforces tool policy. Agent security covers Bedrock, Vertex, Copilot Studio, M365 Copilot, Agentforce.
2.evidence: Just-in-time access: a user requests a tool, an admin approves, and access expires on its own
2.has: MCP Gateway: server inventory, tool policy, just-in-time access, Freeze Agent.
2.lacks: No kernel or host sandbox. Egress control not shown. Gateway allowlist only.

3.reason: Detects agent drift and bypass attempts, opens ServiceNow and Jira tickets, quarantines identities. No host-level blocking.
3.evidence: Freeze ticket: the agent, its violations and the steps to investigate are assigned to the right team
3.has: ITDR with Freeze Agent, identity quarantine, ServiceNow and Jira integrations, Ark AI remediation.
3.lacks: Blocks tool calls and identities, not processes, files or network on hosts.

4.reason: MCP Gateway guardrails block or redact sensitive data and tool-borne prompt injection. No jailbreak or toxicity filters.
4.evidence: Injected instructions: prompt injection caught in tool outputs and descriptions, with blocked tools hidden from the agent
4.has: MCP Gateway guardrails on tool requests and responses. SDK and hooks for custom agents.
4.lacks: No browser extension or third-party gateway integration. No jailbreak, toxicity or hallucination filters.

5.reason: Findings map to OWASP Agentic and LLM Top 10, NIST AI RMF and MITRE ATLAS. Immutable audit log.
5.evidence: Compliance view: passing and failing controls by framework, with the evidence behind each
5.has: Compliance view by framework with evidence. Audit trail. SOC2 PDF reports via Ark AI.
5.lacks: No AIBOM export in CycloneDX. Agent inventory lists models and tools only.

6.reason: No AI red teaming or attack library found. Unosecur focuses on identity governance and runtime control.
6.evidence: Searched: Unosecur red teaming, adversarial testing AI agents, jailbreak. AI Agent Security page lists discover, analyze, audit, remediate, detect only.
6.lacks: No attack library, no multi-turn attacks, no CI/CD red teaming.

7.reason: Governs agents with NHIs and humans. Tool-level policy, just-in-time access and right-sizing. Calls run under a named account.
7.evidence: Create a complete inventory of humans, non-humans, and AI agents that traditional IAM tools often miss.
7.has: Unified Identity Fabric: NHI and agent inventory, MCP Gateway tool policy, just-in-time access.
7.lacks: No per-agent cryptographic identity such as SPIFFE. Agents act under user or service accounts.

8.reason: No model scanning, dataset scanning or AI code scanning found. Repos are used only to discover agents.
8.evidence: Searched: Unosecur model scanning, dataset poisoning, AI SAST, AI code scanning. Only agent discovery from repositories found.
8.lacks: No model file scanning, dataset PII or poisoning scans, or AI SAST.

notes: Unosecur is not acquired. It raised a $5M seed in April 2025 (VentureFriends, DFF Ventures) and is Berlin-based. The secure MCP Gateway was announced January 21, 2026. Ark AI was introduced May 14, 2026 as a natural-language operations layer, and the MCP Gateway page also uses the name Ark AI for the gateway. Its inference runs on-prem. Five agent platform pages exist on the site: Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Salesforce Agentforce. Only the Bedrock and Copilot Studio pages were read in full. 3.1 is yes on medium confidence, from admin API and audit log ingestion plus gateway runtime records. Integrations list ServiceNow, Jira, PagerDuty, Slack, Sumo Logic and Elastic. Splunk and Sentinel were not found. The What is AI-SPM page is a glossary article and was not used as proof. 7.1 is partial because the gateway runs calls under a named user or service account, and a per-agent cryptographic credential is not documented. Module 8 is no after two searches and a read of the product pages.
